page: Amazon Web Services c6id.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem is supported by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache, along with hardware instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering a compute-centric memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features a dedicated 474 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume directly attached to the host, ensuring low-latency disk access for scratch data and temporary storage. The instance includes a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and does not contain dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across varied computational tasks. The instance achieved 1,894.18 in stress-ng single-core and 7,735.64 in multi-core metrics, matched by a Geekbench score of 1,610 single-core and 6,004 multi-core. In memory testing, uncached large-block reads registered 58.2 GB/sec and writes reached 41.95 GB/sec. Database and in-memory operations yielded 7.96 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, accompanied by a 12.34 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Heavy compression tasks showed mixed results, with single-threaded gzip operating within expected bounds while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranked lower. CPU-based medium (7B) language model inference is constrained by core counts, processing prompts at 16.29 tokens per second.

The c6id.2xlarge balances dedicated compute capacity with fast local NVMe storage. It is suitable for batch processing, continuous integration and build systems, web serving layers, and caching or database workloads that benefit from low-latency local NVMe scratch space rather than massive system memory pools.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance utilizing the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor clocked at 3.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, accompanied by 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware configuration integrates a direct-attached 474 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate consistent mid-range execution, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,004, a PassMark CPU score of 11,304.41, and 7.96 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. The instance exhibits throughput constraints under heavy multi-threaded decompression and medium-sized LLM inference workloads. Combining dedicated CPU allocation with high-speed local NVMe storage, the c6id.2xlarge is suited for compilation, static web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and localized data caching.
